newsitem.title: USA: NHL-SHARKS END LOSING STREAK AGAINST STARS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-SHARKS END LOSING STREAK AGAINST STARS.

text.p: Darren Turcotte scored with 21 seconds remaining in the third period and Kelly Hrudey made 23 saves as the San Jose Sharks snapped a four-game losing streak with a 2-1 victory over the Dallas Stars on Monday.

With the game tied 1-1 in the final minute, the Sharks kept the puck deep in the Dallas zone. Turcotte took the puck as it bounced out from a group of skaters and cut across ice, banging it home through the pads of goaltender Andy Moog for his eighth goal.
"I was alone in front ... it was the first shot I had in four games," Turcotte said. "Somehow it sneaked under him (Moog) or between his legs."

In Boston, Troy Mallette's fourth goal of the season, with 6:30 left in regulation tied the score and Bill Ranford made it stand up as the Boston Bruins skated to a 3-3 tie with the Chicago Blackhawks.
Adam Oates added a goal and an assist for the Bruins.
Alexei Zhamnov, Bob Probert and James Black had goals for the Blackhawks.

In Montreal, Daniel Alfredsson tied a career-high with four points on a goal and three assists and Sergei Zholtok and Alexandre Daigle had two goals apiece as the Ottawa Senators routed the Montreal Canadiens, 6-0.
Damian Rhodes turned aside 14 shots for his first shutout of the season and third of his career. He was aided by an Ottawa defence that held the Canadiens to their lowest shot total of the season.
At New Jersey, Martin Brodeur made 37 saves as the New Jersey Devils skated to the first 0-0 tie in team history against the Buffalo Sabres.
Brodeur posted his third shutout of the season and is 15-7-3. The Devils extended their unbeaten streak to seven games (5-0-2) and were without starting defenceman Scott Stevens, who has the flu.
Buffalo's Dominik Hasek also made 37 saves for his fifth shutout of the season.
At The Islanders, Ray Sheppard scored his team-leading 17th goal 1:46 into overtime as the Florida Panthers blew a three-goal lead but recovered for a 4-3 victory over the New York Islanders.

Former Islander Martin Straka was falling down but managed to make a pass to Sheppard, who broke into New York's zone on a 2-on-1 and beat goaltender Eric Fichaud with a wrist shot to the top right corner.
At Tampa Bay, Peter Bondra had a goal and an assist in the first period and Jim Carey stopped 23 shots as the Washington Capitals handed the Tampa Bay Lightning their fourth straight loss, 3-1.
Kelly Miller added an insurance goal in the second period for the Capitals, who won for just the second time in 10 games. Daymond Langkow had the lone goal for Tampa Bay.

In Toronto, Jaromir Jagr had two goals and three assists and Mario Lemieux added a pair of goals and an assist, leading the Pittsburgh Penguins to their third straight win, 6-5 over the Toronto Maple Leafs.

The line of Lemieux, Jagr and Ron Francis have been on a torrid scoring pace with a combined 36 goals and 40 assists in the 15 games since they were put together. Jagr leads the league with 32 goals and 55 points and Lemieux is second with 53 points.
At Colorado, Eric Lacroix scored on a wraparound with 45 seconds left in the third period to lift the Colorado Avalanche to a 4-3 victory over the Calgary Flames.

Lacroix skated behind the net and jammed the puck inside the left post, past goaltender Dwayne Roloson for his 11th marker. Colorado avenged two losses at Calgary this season and improved to 3-0-3 in its last six home meetings with the Flames.
"I saw the puck behind the net," said Lacroix. "Coach emphasised get the puck and put it front and good things will happen. I didn't even see it go in the net.

In Anaheim, Jeremy Roenick scored the tie-breaking goal with 3:43 left in the third period and Nikolai Khabibulin made 37 saves, leading the Phoenix Coyotes their first-ever win in Anaheim, a 2-1 triumph over the Mighty Ducks.
Khabibulin held the Ducks off the scoreboard through the first two periods before Warren Rychel's eighth goal of the season 7:59 into the third period tied it for Anaheim.

In Vancouver, Andre Kovalenko, Ryan Smyth and Dean McAmmond scored two goals apiece and Bob Essensa stopped 26 shots for his 16th career shutout as the Edmonton Oilers snapped a seven-game winless streak with a 7-0 rout of the Vancouver Canucks.
Mats Lindgren also tallied for the Oilers.
